summary:
The Pitcairn Islands stand under the United Kingdom's framework: defence and external affairs are reserved to the United Kingdom, and United Kingdom domestic measures such as the Equality Act 2010 and its 2025 single-sex-services code do not apply here of their own force. Local law governs, and those measures could reach Pitcairn only by Order in Council.

Same-sex sexual activity has been legal in the Pitcairn Islands since 2001.

The Pitcairn Constitution Order 2010 prohibits discrimination on grounds of sexual orientation, and that guarantee has been in force since 2010.

Same-sex marriage has been legal since 14 May 2015. The Same Sex Marriage and Civil Partnerships Ordinance 2015 defines marriage as the union of two people regardless of sex, sexual orientation or gender identity, and it recognises civil partnerships performed outside Pitcairn.

Adoption has been available to same-sex couples since 2015 and is open to married, unmarried and single people alike.

No source in this inventory addresses trans-specific law: legal gender recognition, sex markers on identity documents and entry screening are undocumented for Pitcairn, so a trans visitor has no sourced basis for expecting either a protection or an obstacle on those points.
tangentialFactors:
The resident population is roughly fifty people and none is known to be in a same-sex relationship. On a settlement of that size the absence of visible same-sex couples reflects arithmetic rather than evidence of a documented climate of acceptance or of hostility.

The 2015 ordinance was approved unanimously by the Island Council on 1 April 2015, signed by Governor Jonathan Sinclair on 5 May 2015, published on 13 May 2015 and in force from 14 May 2015.

Military service for the Pitcairn Islands falls under United Kingdom responsibility, so any recruitment or service conditions follow United Kingdom arrangements rather than local rules.
localsOnly:
Residents may marry without regard to sex, sexual orientation or gender identity under the Same Sex Marriage and Civil Partnerships Ordinance 2015, and civil partnerships entered into outside Pitcairn are recognised locally.

Adoption is available to married, unmarried and single residents, with no sexual-orientation condition attached.

The sexual-orientation non-discrimination guarantee in the 2010 Constitution is the standing protection residents can invoke, and family law is made locally by the Island Council rather than by the United Kingdom Parliament.
outOfScopeNotes:
Gender recognition and any change of sex marker on Pitcairn identity documents are not addressed by any source in this inventory. The position is unresolved, not permissive and not restrictive.

No source records hate-crime provisions covering gender identity, and none documents how the 2010 Constitution's discrimination guarantee has been enforced. Complaint outcomes are unknown.

Facilities, healthcare access and screening practice for trans visitors are not documented here. Nothing in the inventory indicates a ban on gender-affirming care or the existence of a dedicated trans service.

Whether the United Kingdom's single-sex-services code has been extended to Pitcairn by Order in Council is not stated in the sources. The extension mechanism exists, but its use for this measure is unresolved.
